Scientists’ profiles: applied fixes and fresh review

Fixes applied

114 of 114 confirmed issues from the previous report were fixed. Your reference to L001–L126 was interpreted as the latest report’s N001–N126 set. Its 12 Needs verification items were excluded, as requested. The 79 older verification items were also retained.

This batch changed 64 distinct English fields, synchronized across 10 files (256 field-level edits). The earlier 272 approved fixes remain in place. All 114 applied edits, their exact files and locations, and complete before/after field values are included in this report.

For N009 and N103, moving quoted journal titles to the ends of sentences also required moving the existing adjacent period inside the closing quotation mark. These two contextual punctuation adjustments are explicitly recorded in the change log.

Scope and method

All 83 corrected English profile names, rendered credentials, fields, titles/affiliations, and biographies were reread. The active sources are i18n/scientists-profiles/chunk-01.json through chunk-04.json; their content matches i18n/scientists-profiles.json and all matching deployment copies. The older unused mapping i18n/scientists-profiles-en.json was not edited.

American English conventions are retained. Ordinary disciplines and descriptive roles use sentence case; ranges use en dashes; commas and periods go inside quotation marks. Foreign qualifications and official names are not converted to assumed American equivalents. Uncertain names, technical relationships, ranks, and factual claims remain verification questions. No external fact-check was performed.

Each row counts as one finding, including a repeated convention within one profile. Consistency is classified as Orthography, Grammar, or Style. The 96 verification questions are excluded from the 51 confirmed-finding category counts. Current excerpts are HTML-decoded and whitespace-normalized, with exact underlying field values provided in the audit. Some new findings concern the context surrounding approved partial replacements; these are identified explicitly.

Exact original field value

<p class="bio bio-lead">Aytekin Huseynli is an international specialist in social policy, social work, child and family welfare. Dr. Huseynli is an assistant professor at the University of Washington. Her applied research focuses on the formulation of social policies, especially the improvement of family and child welfare. Aytekin Huseynli also explores strategies and ways to channel natural resource revenues into social development in countries rich in oil, gas and minerals. Aytekin Huseynli&#x27;s doctoral dissertation led to the creation of the National Children&#x27;s Fund state program, which covers 7 million children in Kazakhstan and is financed by a certain part of the oil and gas wealth.</p><p class="bio">She is the author of 3 chapters in 3 books in the field of social policy, social work and social development, 15 scientific articles in 15 international scientific journals, and more than 20 publications, and she is a member of the editorial board of 2 scientific journals in the field of social development, social policy and social work. She gave presentations at more than 20 international scientific conferences and received 2 international awards for her scientific work. She was the scientific supervisor of more than 10 students. Aytekin Huseynli teaches social research, statistics, program evaluation and social policy. Currently, she is the head of several research projects.</p><p class="bio">A pioneer in her field, Aytekin Huseynli is one of the first professional social workers who received an education in the field of social work in the post-Soviet region and is one of the founders of the social work profession and education in Azerbaijan. She is the founder of the "Azerbaijan Social Work" Public Union, which represents Azerbaijan in the field of international and regional social development.</p><p class="bio">She is a member of the Board of Directors of the Global Program at the Brown School of the University of Washington, the Deputy Director of International Programs at the Center for Social Development, and an Associate Professor at the Center for Child Abuse Research, Training and Education. At the global level, Aytekin Huseynli is a research and statistics specialist for Eurasia at UNICEF, a member of the Research Committee of the International Association of Schools of Social Work.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Head of the &quot;Dynamic Systems&quot; Department at the &quot;Helmholtz&quot; Scientific Research Center, Munich, Germany</p><p class="bio">Rector&#x27;s Distinguished Visiting Professor at Marmara University, Istanbul, Turkey</p><p class="bio">Professor Masud Efendiyev is the first Azerbaijani scientist living abroad, known both for the prestigious international awards he won and the international conferences organized in his honor. He is the first Azerbaijani scientist to win these awards.</li><li>In 2022, he was awarded the honorary title of Honored Scientist by the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev.</li><li>In 2023, he was awarded the Life Achievement Award of the Fields Institute.</li></ul></div><p class="bio-section-title">International conferences and recognition</p><p class="bio">The 60th anniversary of teacher Masud was celebrated in Germany (Munich), and the 70th anniversary was celebrated in Baku (at the state level) with international scientific conferences.</p><p class="bio">75 leading scientists from 25 countries participated in the conference held in Munich.</p><p class="bio">55 famous scientists from 23 countries participated in the conference held in Baku.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Dinara Abbasova is a scientist specializing in nuclear energy, nuclear safety, radioactive waste management and nuclear knowledge preservation. Her main research areas include the study of international standards for radiation chemistry, isotope and biomarker analyses, chromatography technologies, and nuclear material safety. She worked as a consultant at the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), a research scientist at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) Institute for Resource Ecology, an invited professor at the Polish Academy of Sciences, and a director at the ANAS Institute of Radiation Problems. The author of more than 80 scientific articles and presentations, Abbasova has organized and spoken at more than 40 international conferences and prepared e-learning materials for the IAEA and the European Commission. She was awarded &quot;Achievements in Science&quot; (2010), &quot;Young Nuclear Specialist&quot; of IAEA (2012), Simon&#x27;s Fellowship (2015–2020) and OECD/NEA (information-data-knowledge management) expert award (2022). She is a member of the "Women in Nuclear" organization and a nuclear safety expert for the IAEA Expert Network and the European Commission.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Dr. Vahid Garousi works in two professional roles: as an IT specialist and an IT professor. Since 1998 he has provided consulting and training to international IT companies in software engineering, testing and QA, and he is also a Professor of Software Engineering at Queen&#x27;s University in Belfast, United Kingdom. At the same time, he serves as a part-time Software Test Strategist and Team Leader at ProSys LLC in Azerbaijan and Testinium A.Ş. in Turkey. His name is written in English as Vahid Garousi.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi earned his Ph.D. in Software Engineering from Carleton University in Canada in 2006 and his master&#x27;s degree from the University of Waterloo in Canada in 2003. Over more than 25 years of IT experience, he served as the lead test and QA consultant for the United Kingdom&#x27;s COVID mobile application in 2020–2021, as a test consultant for one of the UK&#x27;s major banks in 2022, and as the lead test and QA consultant at HAVELSAN in Turkey from 2012 to 2019.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi is a Professor of Software Engineering at Queen&#x27;s University in Belfast, United Kingdom. Previously he held associate professor positions in the Netherlands (2017–2019), Turkey (2015–2017) and Canada (2001–2014). He received his Ph.D. in Software Engineering from Carleton University in Canada in 2006. His research areas are software engineering, software testing, empirical studies, action research and industry–academia collaboration. In parallel with his academic career, he is a practicing consultant and trainer in software engineering, delivering consulting and corporate training across various areas including software engineering, testing and quality assurance, model-driven development and software maintenance.</p><p class="bio">In a bibliometric study published in the Journal of Systems and Software in 2018, Dr. Garousi was ranked the 8th most active mid-career software engineering researcher in the world, out of more than 4,000 active researchers. Dr. Garousi has published more than 150 papers to date. He was selected as a Distinguished Speaker by the IEEE Computer Society in 2012–2015. He is also a member of the IEEE and the IEEE Computer Society and a licensed professional engineer (PEng) in Alberta, Canada.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Garousi has been the Principal Investigator of several research projects and has launched many significant R&amp;D software engineering projects together with software companies in several countries, including Canada and Turkey. He has served as an organizer and program committee member at many international conferences, such as ICST, ICSP, CSEE&amp;T, MoDELS and the Turkish National Software Engineering Conference. Among the awards he has received is the Alberta Ingenuity New Faculty Award, which he won in 2007.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Scientific achievements and recognition:</p><div <p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli is a poet, translator, scholar and public figure. In addition to his extensive research in Azerbaijani literature, linguistics and journalism, he is also known internationally for diaspora activity and academic cooperation. With his scientific work "Comparison of Verb Structures in Estonian and Turkish Languages," he is the first Azerbaijani scholar to investigate kinship relations between Finno-Ugric and Turkic-Tatar languages in world linguistics.</p><p class="bio-section-title">Main research areas</p><p class="bio-section-title">Turkology and linguistics:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Comparison of Verb Structures in Estonian and Turkish Languages&quot;</li><li>&quot;Linguistic relations and structural differences between Turkish and Estonian&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Political and cultural relations:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Political and cultural relations between Estonia and the Turkic World&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Journalism and visual media:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;The importance of photography in the print media&quot;</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Awards and honorary titles:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>&quot;Progress&quot; medal (2022) – awarded by the President of Azerbaijan for his contribution to the development of the Azerbaijani diaspora.</li><li>&quot;Golden Star Medal&quot; (2024) – awarded by the International Academy of Sciences for Turkic World Studies of the Republic of Turkey.</li><li>Medal &quot;For service in diaspora activity&quot; (2024) – presented by the State Committee on Work with Diaspora of the Republic of Azerbaijan.</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Publications and literary activity:</p><p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli is the author of both scholarly-journalistic articles and works of poetry and prose. His works have been translated into Estonian, Georgian, Russian, Latvian, German, English and Turkic languages.</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>author of more than 40 socio-political, historical and scientific-cultural articles,</li><li>6 books and 1 monograph,</li><li>author of 4 scientific articles published in 2 scientific journals.</li><li>speaker and participant at more than 20 international symposia and conferences.</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Professional and academic activity:</p><ul class="awards-list"><li>Finno-Ugric and Turkic Peoples Research Center – chairman</li><li>University of Tartu (Estonia) – director of the Turkish Language Center</li><li>World Congress of Azerbaijanis – member of the Board, deputy chairman</li><li>Estonian-Azerbaijani Society – chairman</li><li>World Association of Azerbaijani Scientists – member of the Organizing Committee</li><li>Azerbaijan Writers&#x27; Union – member</li><li>Estonian Society of Academic Orientalists – member</li><li>Turkish Literature Foundation – honorary member</li></ul><p class="bio-section-title">Diplomatic and translation activity:</p><p class="bio">Khagani Gayibli has participated as a translator in high-level official meetings in Estonia and Turkey. He served as special interpreter during official visits by the presidents, parliament speakers and ministers of Azerbaijan, Turkey and Estonia.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">In 2019, she obtained a Ph.D. degree in Materials Chemistry from the University of Orleans, France. Her research areas include structure-property relations of polymer materials, nanostructuring, preparation of functional materials and application of these fields in modern technologies. She collaborated with numerous international laboratories and conducted postdoctoral research at the French ENSAM/PIMM laboratory and the University of Delaware in the United States. Aynur Guliyeva also has industrial experience - she worked as a project manager for medicinal capsules for 2 years at Capsugel, which is part of the Lonza company. She currently works as an assistant professor at the university. Alongside her teaching, she has established a research group on "smart polymer materials" and conducts research in this field. She also performs various teaching and administrative duties at the university and mentors female scientists to support their professional development. Aynur Guliyeva has a number of scientific articles and has made oral and poster presentations at international conferences.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">He is an expert in operations research and mathematical modeling. From 1999 to 2024, he taught more than 25 different Ph.D., master&#x27;s and bachelor&#x27;s courses at York and Toronto Universities in Canada. In 2013, he was awarded the Excellence in Teaching Award by the Faculty of Science at the University of York – an award given to him for teaching excellence and service to the faculty. Together with Professor Robert G. Burns, he translated the works of N. N. Moiseyev, a former academician of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR, &quot;Man and the Noosphere&quot; and &quot;How Far Tomorrow is&quot; into English. The translation of the last book was published by Birkhauser publishing house in 2022.</p>

In 2024, he was awarded the medal of the Republic of Azerbaijan &quot;For services in diaspora activities&quot; for his activities in the field of international relations and diaspora.</p>

<p class="bio bio-lead">Akif Alaferdov is a well-known traumatologist, a descendant of Azerbaijanis who were deported to Kyrgyzstan in 1933.</p><p class="bio">Dr. Akif made important contributions to the methodology of surgical treatment of femoral neck fractures. McMurray received a patent for the invention of the &quot;detachable fixator&quot; used in surgery. Akif Alaferdov is the author of a monograph, more than 35 scientific articles, 3 methodical materials and more than 20 effective recommendations on the treatment of femoral neck fractures with surgical intervention.</p><p class="bio">During his professional career, Alaferdov was the head of the complex trauma department at the National Hospital of the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic and a member of the Special Scientific Council of the Kyrgyz State Medical Institute. He has performed thousands of operations and trained highly qualified specialists. His contributions in this field were recognized by the President of the Kyrgyz Republic with an Honorary Order in 1997, and in 2003 he was awarded the title of "Honored Doctor."</p><p class="bio">In addition to his achievements in the field of medicine, Alaferdov was also engaged in social and cultural activities. From 1997 to 2013, he was the chairman of the &quot;Azeri&quot; Public Union of Azerbaijanis living in Kyrgyzstan. Under his leadership, Sunday schools in the Azerbaijani language were opened, mosques were built, and a folklore ensemble called &quot;Stars&quot; was created. He took part in many events to strengthen the relations between Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan and organized &quot;Bishkek-Baku&quot; telebridges for many years with the participation of deputies, writers, public figures and diaspora representatives representing both sides.</p><p class="bio">For his long-term public activity, Akif Alaferdov was awarded the &quot;Dank&quot; state award in 2008, as well as the medal &quot;For service in Diaspora activity&quot; from the State Committee for Work with the Diaspora of the Republic of Azerbaijan. In 2023, he was awarded the Order of &quot;Friend&quot; by the President of Kyrgyzstan for his contributions to strengthening peace, friendship and cooperation between nations. He was awarded the &quot;Chingiz Aytmatov&quot; medal for his achievements in the fields of culture, science, literature and social activities.</p><p class="bio">He was awarded the &quot;Progress&quot; medal in 2026 by order of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Mr. Ilham Aliyev for his services in the field of strengthening friendship between peoples and the development of the Azerbaijani diaspora.</p><div class="card-resources"><a class="btn btn-primary" href="akif-alaferdov-media.html">Additional resources <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></a></div>

<p class="bio bio-lead">He completed his undergraduate and postgraduate studies at the Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics of the Moscow State University named after M. V. Lomonosov.</p><p class="bio">He is a well-known Soviet, Russian and Azerbaijani scientist in the field of development of mathematical models and methods for the study of wave and oscillation processes in the creation of piezoelectric devices and apparatus used in the world ocean and outer space research, marine seismic exploration, electronics, defense and medical industries.</p><p class="bio">For the first time, he managed to solve the problem of determining the optimal shape of piezoelectric elements, which has not been solved for many years, meets the physical properties required in the dynamic mode, and has a minimum mass or volume. The solution to this problem made it possible to determine the location and individual characteristics of objects moving under water in the world ocean, the information of interest to experts in relevant scientific fields was recorded from space objects - artificial satellites and spaceships, and the creation of receiver-transmitter devices to transmit and receive the Flight Control Center. For the first time, he successfully applied the method of solving two- and three-dimensional dynamic problems, which are important in the creation of piezoelectric devices used in military equipment. The existence of the &quot;edge effect&quot; in disk-shaped piezoceramic membranes was also theoretically discovered by him for the first time. The piezoceramic actuator, developed jointly with the co-authors, was successfully used to solve the problem of creating an artificial heart. He is the author of more than 450 open and closed (confidential) scientific works, inventions, monographs, higher education textbooks, a number of scientific articles on the problems of organizing higher professional education and educational technologies. Under his scientific guidance, 7 graduate students, including 3 Azerbaijanis, defended their candidate dissertations. In general, based on the obtained scientific results, he delivered more than 60 presentations, including 12 commissioned plenary presentations, at 30 international and general congresses, conferences and symposia.</p><p class="bio">Some of the prizes and awards received by Professor Aladdin Allahverdiyev for his achievements in the fields of science, technology and education:</p><p class="bio">Medal named after the Hero of Socialist Labor of the Russian Cosmonautics Federation, lieutenant general, Lenin Prize laureate, professor, chairman of the State Commission on Space Programs Georgy Alexandrovich Tyulin;</p><p class="bio">Medal named after Khalil Ahmadovich Rakhmatulin, Hero of Socialist Labor of the National Committee for Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, academician, laureate of four Orders of Lenin, several State Prizes;</p><p class="bio">the title &quot;Honored worker of higher vocational education of the Russian Federation&quot;;</p><p class="bio">Three times - in 1975, 1977 and 1980 - badges of &quot;The winner of the race of socialism&quot; established by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, the former Council of Ministers of the USSR, the Central Committee of Trade Unions, the Central Committee of the All-Union Labor Party;</p><p class="bio">&quot;850th anniversary of Moscow&quot; state medal;</p><p class="bio">Jubilee medal &quot;250th anniversary of MSU named after M.V. Lomonosov&quot;;</p><p class="bio">Gold medal of the All-Russian Exhibition Center;</p><p class="bio">diploma of the winner of the review-competition of the Presidium of the Central Office of the All-Union Scientific Medical-Technical Society;</p><p class="bio">4 years in a row (2001–2004) laureate titles and cash prizes of the &quot;Moscow Grant&quot; competition established by the Moscow Government for science and technology in the field of education;</p><p class="bio">Numerous honorary decrees, diplomas, certificates, etc. of the Russian Federation, some foreign countries, many international institutions, organizations.</p>
